title: Bunionectomy: what happens next?
intro:
Here's a first draft of the bunionectomy game, built from your outline. Each step shows what the students would see, the question "What happens next?", and the instrument they should pick. The pictures are cartoon drawings that change as the case moves along.

**Nothing here is final.** Every instrument answer is a **proposal** until you OK it. Anything marked **Instructor confirmation needed** is a detail I didn't want to guess.

For each step, tap **Looks right** or **Needs a change** (add a note if you like). The **Questions for you** at the bottom are the main thing I need before building. Most are one tap.
outline_notes: **"Osteotomy to remove exostosis":** taking off the bump is usually called an *exostectomy* (or medial eminence resection). "Osteotomy" usually means a corrective cut through the metatarsal to realign it. If your technique includes a corrective osteotomy, it should be its own step (step 11 below is a placeholder for it).
**"Realign joint and fixate with screws":** screws usually fix a bone cut (osteotomy), not the joint itself. The exception is a fusion like the Lapidus. Which one applies changes the fixation steps.
**"Release soft tissues":** which tissues, through which incision, and when? Some surgeons release before the bone work, some after.

**Not in the outline but part of the tech's job:** tourniquet, temporary pin with an x-ray check, and the closing count before closure. I added the count as its own step. The others are questions below.
**Opening the capsule** is part of "dissection" in I/H/D/R. I split it out (step 5) so students learn it as a separate moment.

steps.title: Skin incision
steps.sees: Foot prepped and draped. The incision line is marked over the inside (medial) side of the big toe joint.

wrong.label: Metzenbaum scissors
wrong.why: Scissors dissect tissue once the skin is open. They don't make the skin incision.

wrong.label: Electrosurgical pencil (Bovie)
wrong.why: Used for bleeders after the incision is made.

wrong.label: Freer elevator
wrong.why: Lifts tissue off bone, which comes much later.

steps.why_right: The skin incision is made with the scalpel. The tech passes it safely (handle first, or using a neutral zone if that's facility policy).
steps.after_text: The marked line becomes an incision and small bleeders appear.

steps.title: Hemostasis
steps.sees: Small bleeders along the skin edges.
steps.alternatives: cautery, electrocautery, Bovie; mosquito hemostat + tie for a larger vessel

wrong.label: Bulb syringe
wrong.why: Irrigation clears the field but doesn't stop bleeding.

wrong.label: Suture scissors
wrong.why: Nothing to cut yet, since no suture has been placed.

wrong.label: Rongeur
wrong.why: Bites bone. It has nothing to do with bleeding.

steps.why_right: Cautery seals small vessels. The tech keeps the tip clean between uses.
steps.after_text: The red spots disappear.
confirm: Is a tourniquet up? (much less bleeding if so)

steps.title: Dissection to the capsule
steps.sees: Fatty tissue under the skin. The joint capsule is underneath. A small skin nerve runs nearby.
steps.action: Dissect down through the subcutaneous tissue to the joint capsule.
steps.alternatives: Metz, pickups, tissue forceps, tenotomy scissors

wrong.label: Curved Mayo scissors
wrong.why: Built for heavy tissue. Too coarse for fine dissection near a nerve.

wrong.label: Osteotome & mallet
wrong.why: Cuts bone. We're still in soft tissue.

wrong.label: Needle holder
wrong.why: Drives suture needles, which is for closure.

steps.why_right: Fine scissors and toothed forceps let the surgeon spread and cut the soft tissue carefully.
steps.after_text: The wound opens and the capsule shows at the bottom.

steps.title: Retraction
steps.sees: The skin edges keep falling back over the capsule.
steps.action: Hold the skin and soft tissue open for exposure.

wrong.label: Deaver retractor
wrong.why: A large abdominal retractor, far too big for a foot.

wrong.label: Richardson retractor
wrong.why: Made for deep abdominal wounds. Wrong scale.

wrong.label: Towel clip
wrong.why: Holds drapes, not tissue.

steps.why_right: Small handheld retractors (or a small self-retainer) suit a small foot incision.
steps.after_text: Retractors pull the edges apart.
confirm: Which small retractors are on your tray
Does the tech hold retractors in your setup?

steps.title: Open the capsule
steps.sees: The joint capsule is exposed over the bump.

wrong.label: Bone rasp
wrong.why: Smooths bone, but the bone isn't exposed yet.

wrong.label: Needle holder
wrong.why: Closure instrument.

wrong.label: K-wire driver
wrong.why: Pins bone after it's been realigned.

steps.why_right: The capsule is cut with the scalpel to reach the bone.
steps.after_text: The capsule opens and bone shows underneath.

steps.title: Expose the bump
steps.sees: The capsule is open, but tissue is still stuck to the bump.
steps.action: Lift the capsule and periosteum off the bump.

wrong.label: Adson forceps
wrong.why: Grasps tissue but can't lift it cleanly off bone.

wrong.label: Mosquito hemostat
wrong.why: Clamps small bleeders.

wrong.label: Suture scissors
wrong.why: Only for cutting suture.

steps.why_right: An elevator peels soft tissue off the bone so the bump is fully exposed.
steps.after_text: The bump (medial eminence) is fully exposed.

steps.title: Retraction around the bone
steps.sees: The bone is exposed, but the soft tissue needs protecting before any cutting.
steps.action: Place bone retractors around the metatarsal head to protect the soft tissue.

wrong.label: Skin hook
wrong.why: Holds skin edges but won't protect tissue around bone from the saw.

wrong.label: Deaver retractor
wrong.why: Far too big.

wrong.label: Mosquito hemostat
wrong.why: Not a retractor.

steps.why_right: Hohmanns lever around the bone, holding soft tissue clear of the saw. Retraction comes back here, deeper this time.
steps.after_text: Retractor tips cup the bone.
confirm: Are Hohmanns used in this case?

steps.title: Remove the bump
steps.sees: The bump is exposed and protected.
steps.alternatives: power saw, micro-sagittal saw; osteotome & mallet

wrong.label: Drill
wrong.why: Makes holes for screws, not cuts.

wrong.label: Rongeur
wrong.why: Close! It trims and smooths after the cut, but doesn't make it.

wrong.label: Needle holder
wrong.why: Closure instrument.

steps.why_right: The saw makes the cut. The tech may drip saline on the blade to keep the bone from overheating.
steps.after_text: A cut line appears and the bump comes off.
confirm: Does the tech irrigate during the cut?
Is this cut separate from a corrective osteotomy? (see step 11)

steps.title: Smooth the edge
steps.sees: The cut edge of the bone is rough.

wrong.label: Scalpel
wrong.why: Cuts soft tissue, not bone.

wrong.label: Depth gauge
wrong.why: Measures screw holes, which comes later.

wrong.label: Mosquito hemostat
wrong.why: Clamps bleeders.

steps.why_right: A rasp or rongeur leaves a smooth edge so it won't irritate the tissue.
steps.after_text: The edge is smooth, with bone dust left behind.

steps.title: Irrigation
steps.sees: Bone dust and debris in the wound.

wrong.label: Sponge
wrong.why: Dabs blood but won't wash out bone dust.

wrong.label: Electrosurgical pencil
wrong.why: Controls bleeding, doesn't clean.

wrong.label: Bone rasp
wrong.why: Makes more bone dust!

steps.why_right: Saline washes out bone debris, which helps prevent irritation and infection. Irrigation comes back again at closure.
steps.after_text: The field is clean and wet.

steps.title: Corrective osteotomy (only if your technique includes it)
steps.sees: The bump is gone, but the metatarsal is still angled.
steps.action: Make the corrective cut through the metatarsal.

wrong.label: Drill
wrong.why: Holes come after the cut is made and positioned.

wrong.label: Rongeur
wrong.why: Trims bone but can't make a clean corrective cut.

wrong.label: Scalpel
wrong.why: Soft tissue only.

steps.why_right: Placeholder: only included if the technique you teach has a corrective osteotomy.
steps.after_text: A corrective cut line appears in the bone.
confirm: Is a corrective osteotomy part of this lesson at all?
Which one, and where does it fall in the sequence?

steps.title: Release the tight tissue
steps.sees: The big toe is still pulled toward the second toe by tight tissue on the outside of the joint.
steps.action: Release the tight lateral soft tissues.
steps.alternatives: tenotomy scissors; small blade (Instructor confirmation needed)

wrong.label: Sagittal saw
wrong.why: This step is soft tissue, not bone.

wrong.label: Rongeur
wrong.why: Bites bone.

wrong.label: K-wire driver
wrong.why: Pins come after the toe is realigned.

steps.why_right: Cutting the tight tissue lets the toe swing back into line.
steps.after_text: The release site is marked between the first and second toes.
confirm: Same incision or a separate one between the 1st and 2nd toes? (A separate one adds another incision, hemostasis and retraction.)

steps.title: Realign and pin
steps.sees: The toe is now loose enough to straighten.
steps.action: Hold the corrected position with a temporary pin.

wrong.label: Drill
wrong.why: Close, but the position is held before drilling for screws.

wrong.label: Screwdriver & screw
wrong.why: Comes after the hole is drilled and measured.

wrong.label: Osteotome & mallet
wrong.why: Cuts bone. We're holding it now, not cutting.

steps.why_right: A temporary wire holds the alignment so the surgeon can check it (often on x-ray) before final fixation.
steps.after_text: The toe straightens and the pin shows.
confirm: Fluoroscopy (C-arm) check, and lead for the team?

steps.title: Drill for the screw
steps.sees: The alignment is held and confirmed.
steps.action: Drill the pilot hole for the screw.
steps.alternatives: drill bit, pilot drill; cannulated drill over a guide wire

wrong.label: Screwdriver & screw
wrong.why: The hole has to be drilled and measured first.

wrong.label: Depth gauge
wrong.why: You measure after you drill.

wrong.label: K-wire driver
wrong.why: The pin is already in.

steps.why_right: Drill, then measure, then screw. Anticipating that order is the whole point here.
steps.after_text: A drill hole appears.
confirm: Bit size (set by the system, not guessed)

steps.title: Measure
steps.sees: The pilot hole is drilled.

wrong.label: Screwdriver & screw
wrong.why: You can't pick the screw until you know the length.

wrong.label: Drill
wrong.why: Already drilled.

wrong.label: Bone rasp
wrong.why: Smoothing is long done.

steps.why_right: The depth gauge gives the length. The tech listens for the number and gets that screw ready.
steps.after_text: No change. The surgeon calls out a length.
confirm: Any countersink or tap step before the screw? (depends on the system)

steps.title: Insert the screw
steps.sees: The surgeon calls the screw length.
steps.action: Load the correct screw and pass it for insertion.

wrong.label: Drill
wrong.why: The hole is already drilled.

wrong.label: Needle holder
wrong.why: Closure instrument.

wrong.label: K-wire driver
wrong.why: Temporary pin, not final fixation.

steps.why_right: The tech confirms the length, loads the screw, and makes sure the implant gets recorded.
steps.after_text: Screws in, temporary pin out.
confirm: How many screws (drill, measure, screw repeats for each)
Implant documentation steps you want included

steps.title: Final irrigation
steps.sees: Fixation is done and the wound has debris in it.

wrong.label: Needle holder
wrong.why: Closure comes after irrigation and hemostasis.

wrong.label: Dressing
wrong.why: The very last thing.

wrong.label: Sagittal saw
wrong.why: Bone work is done.

steps.why_right: One last flush before closing. Irrigation comes back here.
steps.after_text: The field is clean and wet.

steps.title: Hemostasis before closure
steps.sees: A little oozing.

wrong.label: Suture scissors
wrong.why: Nothing to cut yet.

wrong.label: Bone rasp
wrong.why: Bone work is done.

wrong.label: Towel clip
wrong.why: Holds drapes.

steps.why_right: Bleeding is checked again before closing. Hemostasis comes back here.
steps.after_text: Field dry.
confirm: Is the tourniquet let down before closure in your technique?

steps.title: Closing count
steps.sees: The surgeon is about to close.
steps.action: Start the closing count with the circulator: sponges, sharps, instruments.

wrong.label: Get the dressing ready
wrong.why: Fine to prep, but the count comes first.

wrong.label: Scalpel
wrong.why: No more cutting.

wrong.label: Sagittal saw
wrong.why: Bone work is done.

steps.why_right: Counting before closure protects the patient from a retained item. Starting it is the tech's job.
steps.after_text: Count correct, so closure can begin.
confirm: Your facility's count policy and timing

steps.title: Close the capsule
steps.sees: Count correct. The capsule is open over the bone.

wrong.label: Mosquito hemostat
wrong.why: Clamps vessels. Not for driving needles.

wrong.label: Metzenbaum scissors
wrong.why: Dissecting scissors aren't used in closure.

wrong.label: Rongeur
wrong.why: Bone instrument.

steps.why_right: The tech loads the needle holder and passes it ready to use, along with forceps.
steps.after_text: Capsule stitched closed.
confirm: Suture type and size for each layer

steps.title: Cut the suture
steps.sees: Knot tied.

wrong.label: Metzenbaum scissors
wrong.why: Never cut suture with Metz scissors. It dulls them.

wrong.label: Scalpel
wrong.why: Not used to cut suture tails.

wrong.label: Mosquito hemostat
wrong.why: Doesn't cut.

steps.why_right: Suture scissors (or straight Mayos) for suture. A classic teaching point.
steps.after_text: Tails trimmed.

steps.title: Close the skin
steps.sees: Deep layers closed. The skin is still open.

wrong.label: Electrosurgical pencil
wrong.why: Doesn't close skin.

wrong.label: Hohmann retractor
wrong.why: Bone retractor, done with it.

wrong.label: Bulb syringe
wrong.why: Irrigation is done.

steps.why_right: Skin closure is the final layer.
steps.after_text: The incision is stitched closed.
confirm: Skin suture vs. staples, and type

steps.title: Dressing
steps.sees: The skin is closed.
steps.action: Apply the dressing, holding the toe in its corrected position.
steps.alternatives: non-adherent layer, gauze, roll gauze, elastic wrap

wrong.label: Towel clip
wrong.why: Drapes come off after the dressing, not before.

wrong.label: Counted sponge
wrong.why: Counted sponges aren't used as the dressing.

wrong.label: Bulb syringe
wrong.why: Irrigation is done.

steps.why_right: The dressing protects the incision and helps hold the correction.
steps.after_text: The foot is wrapped.

options: Leave it out of the game

questions.text: Where is the soft tissue release done?
options: Separate incision between the 1st and 2nd toes
Cannulated screws over a guide wire
Pick one of four (like this draft)
Pick everything needed from a tray
Start with pick-one, add the tray later
